Teaching a sourdough starter to keep a diary

Posted on 17 November 2024 by Hal Brindlecombe

For about three months I have been logging the temperature and rise of the starter that lives on top of my fridge. It started as a joke, then became a small spreadsheet, and is now a tiny sensor taped to the side of a jam jar.

This post walks through the setup, what went wrong, and the one surprising pattern that turned up in the data.

The hardware

The sensor is a cheap time-of-flight distance module pointing down at the surface of the dough. Every ten minutes it records how far the surface is from the lid, alongside a temperature reading from a probe tucked under the jar.

  • One microcontroller with built-in wireless
  • One distance sensor, mounted in a lid I drilled myself
  • One temperature probe and a lot of tape

The software

The logging script is deliberately boring. It wakes up, takes both readings, and appends a line to a file on a small home server:

reading = sensor.distance_mm()
temp = probe.celsius()
log.append(timestamp(), reading, temp)

Once a week I copy the file across and plot it. I tried a dashboard for a while, but it mostly encouraged me to stare at a jar.

What went wrong

The first version fogged up. Condensation on the inside of the lid made the distance readings jump around wildly overnight. A small ring of absorbent cloth fixed most of it, and a software filter that ignores sudden spikes fixed the rest.

Lesson learned: anything that lives above fermenting dough will eventually be covered in fermenting dough.

The surprising pattern

The starter rises noticeably faster on days when the heating comes on in the morning, which is not surprising, but it also rises faster on the day after I feed it with a particular bag of rye flour. I have no good explanation yet. My current theory is that the bag simply contains more bran, and the yeast enjoys it.

Next month I plan to run a slightly more careful comparison, alternating flours and keeping the kitchen at a steadier temperature. If anything interesting comes out of it, there will be another post, and probably another chart.
